name: IAPP Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional

fee.note: USD 799 for non-members, which includes the first certification maintenance fee; IAPP members pay USD 649 (membership is USD 295 a year). The exam must be taken within one year of purchase.

exam.format: 100 multiple-choice questions (some multi-select or scenario-based) in 2.75 hours, with an optional 15-minute break at the halfway point. Taken online through Pearson VUE OnVUE or at a Pearson VUE test center, in English. The certification term is two years; keeping it needs 20 continuing-education credits and a maintenance fee (USD 250 per term for non-members, covered by IAPP membership).

discounts.text: IAPP members pay USD 649 instead of USD 799.
Holders of another IAPP certification and candidates retaking AIGP get a discounted price (USD 625 for non-members in the IAPP store).

access.retake: A retake is a new exam purchase at the discounted retake price, and it cannot be scheduled sooner than seven days after the previous attempt.
access.accommodations: Request special accommodations (for example extra time or a separate room) when scheduling, with a form completed by a licensed health care provider; approval can take up to 30 days and not every accommodation works with online testing.

scope: Responsible AI governance, legal and framework context, lifecycle risk and organizational implementation.
ai_policy: Check the current assessment rules. AI-assisted study does not imply permission during the exam.
caveats: The AIGP Body of Knowledge v2.1 (effective February 2, 2026) gives a minimum and maximum number of questions per domain instead of percentage weights: I, foundations of AI governance, 16–20; II, laws, standards and frameworks, 19–23; III, governing AI development, 21–25; IV, governing AI deployment and use, 21–25.
The IAPP's pages read for this entry don't say how many of the 100 questions are scored.
IAPP exams are updated every year, and the IAPP announces body of knowledge changes at least 90 days before they reach the exam.
